chole-bhature.title: Chole Bhature (Punjabi Chickpea Curry with Puffed Bread)
steps: Knead flour with yogurt, salt, a pinch of baking soda, and warm water. Rest the dough in a warm place for 2 hours to rise.
Boil soaked chickpeas with a black tea bag (to give dark color) until tender.
Heat oil in a pan. Sauté chopped onions, ginger, and garlic paste until golden-brown.
Add tomato paste, boiled chickpeas, salt, and chole masala spices. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes until gravy is thick.
Roll out dough into large oval flat discs. Deep fry in extremely hot oil, pressing down gently until they inflate like large puffed balloons. Serve hot with Chole.

garlic-naan.title: Tandoori Garlic Naan (Indian Garlic Flatbread)
steps: Knead flour with yogurt, salt, baking powder, a pinch of sugar, and warm water. Rest the dough for 1 hour.
Divide dough into equal balls. Roll them into large teardrop-shaped flatbreads using a rolling pin.
Press minced garlic and chopped cilantro firmly into the top surface of the rolled flatbreads.
Brush the bottom surface of the naan with water (this helps it stick to the pan to mimic a tandoor).

Place the wet side down on a hot iron skillet (tawa). Cook until bubbles start forming on the surface. Flip the skillet upside down directly over the open gas flame to char the garlic side for 1 minute.
Carefully slide off the naan, brush immediately with melted butter, and serve hot.

samosa.title: Classic Punjabi Samosa (Savory Potato Pastry)
steps: Knead flour with carom seeds, salt, 4 tbsp oil, and cold water into a very stiff dough. Rest covered for 30 minutes.
Prepare filling: Heat oil, temper cumin seeds. Add ginger paste, green chili, potatoes, coriander powder, turmeric, and salt. Cook for 5 minutes and let cool.
Divide dough into balls. Roll each into a thin 7-inch circle. Cut the circle exactly in half into two semi-circles.
Fold each semi-circle into a neat cone, brushing water along the straight edge to seal the seam.
Stuff the cone with the cool potato filling, pleat the back edge, and pinch the bottom shut securely.
Deep fry in medium-low oil (crucial to prevent bubbles on crust) for 12-15 minutes until beautifully golden and crispy. Serve with sweet tamarind chutney.

aloo-gobi.title: Aloo Gobi (Potato & Cauliflower Dry Stir-Fry)
steps: Heat oil in a pan. Temper cumin seeds, then sauté onions and half the ginger until soft.
Add potato cubes and cauliflower florets. Stir-fry on medium heat for 3-4 minutes.
Add turmeric, coriander powder, chili powder, and salt. Mix thoroughly to coat the vegetables.
Lower heat, sprinkle 2 tbsp water, cover tightly, and let steam for 10-12 minutes until potatoes are perfectly tender.
Uncover, stir-fry on high heat for 1 minute to dry any moisture, garnish with remaining ginger juliennes and fresh cilantro, and serve.

rajma.title: Rajma Chawal (Punjabi Kidney Bean Curry)
steps: Boil soaked kidney beans in water with a pinch of salt until perfectly tender and soft.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pot. Sauté chopped onions, ginger, and garlic paste until golden-brown.
Add tomato paste, cumin powder, turmeric, salt, and chili powder. Cook until oil separates from the masala.
Add the boiled kidney beans along with their cooking liquid. Mash a few beans to thicken the curry.
Cover and simmer on medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes until the gravy is rich, thick, and well integrated.
Stir in garam masala and serve hot over plain steamed basmati rice.

malai-kofta.title: Malai Kofta (Potato-Cheese Dumplings in Creamy Gravy)
steps: Mix grated paneer, mashed potatoes, flour, a pinch of salt, and cardamom. Knead into a smooth dough.
Shape into small round balls (Kofta). Deep fry in hot oil until golden-brown and crispy, then set aside.
For the Gravy: Heat 1 tbsp oil. Sauté pureed onion, ginger paste, and cardamoms until raw smell disappears (do not brown).
Add cashew paste, tomato paste, a pinch of sugar, and salt. Simmer gently for 8 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream to achieve a smooth, velvety white-orange gravy.
Arrange the crispy Kofta dumplings on a plate and pour the hot creamy gravy right over them (do not simmer kofta in the gravy, as they will dissolve). Serve hot.

massaman-curry.title: Kaeng Matsaman (Thai Massaman Beef Curry)
steps: In a pot, boil beef cubes in 1 cup of coconut milk diluted with 1 cup of water until tender (about 30 minutes). Set aside.
In another pan, fry the thick cream from the top of the remaining coconut milk until it separates and releases oil.
Add 3 tbsp Massaman curry paste to the oil and stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Combine the fried curry paste with the cooked beef and its cooking liquid. Add potato cubes and roasted peanuts.
Simmer on medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes until the potatoes are cooked and tender.
Season with fish sauce, palm sugar, and tamarind paste. Simmer for 2 minutes and serve hot.

pad-krapow.title: Pad Krapow Gai (Stir-Fried Chicken with Holy Basil)
steps: Use a mortar and pestle to pound the garlic and green chilies together into a coarse paste.
In a small bowl, mix light soy sauce, oyster sauce (if available), fish sauce, sugar, and 1 tbsp water.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok on high heat. Add the crushed chili-garlic paste and stir-fry for 30 seconds until highly pungent (watch the smoke!).
Add minced chicken, stir-frying vigorously and breaking up clumps with a spatula until the chicken is almost cooked.
Pour in the sauce mixture and toss on high heat for 1 minute until liquid reduces and coats the chicken.
Turn off the heat. Immediately throw in the fresh holy basil leaves and toss until wilted from the residual heat. Serve with a crispy fried egg on rice.

som-tum.title: Som Tum (Thai Spicy Green Papaya Salad)
steps: In a large clay mortar, crush the garlic and green bird's eye chilies coarsly with a wooden pestle.
Add the roasted peanuts and bruise them slightly (do not crush them completely).
Add palm sugar, fish sauce, lime juice, and a slice of lime peel. Bruise and mix to dissolve the sugar.
Throw in the shredded green mango/papaya substitute along with halved cherry tomatoes and long beans (if available).
Use a spoon in one hand and the pestle in the other to lightly pound and toss the shredded greens, allowing them to absorb the dressing. Serve cold.

tom-kha-gai.title: Tom Kha Gai (Thai Coconut Chicken Soup)
steps: In a pot, combine 1 cup of light chicken stock, sliced galangal, bruised lemongrass, and torn kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a boil for 3 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer (do not boil hard, to prevent coconut milk from separating).
Add sliced chicken breast and button mushrooms. Simmer gently for 5 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Season with fish sauce and a pinch of sugar. Remove from heat.
Stir in the fresh lime juice (off heat) and green bird's eye chilies to taste. Garnish with cilantro and serve warm.

khao-pad.title: Khao Pad Gai (Thai Chicken Fried Rice)
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok on high heat. Sauté minced garlic for 30 seconds.
Add sliced chicken and onions. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Push ingredients to one side of the wok. Pour in the eggs, scramble them lightly until mostly set, then mix with the chicken.
Add the cold Jasmine rice. Drizzle with light soy sauce, a pinch of sugar, and salt.
Toss and stir-fry rapidly on maximum heat for 2 minutes, breaking up rice clumps, until rice is slightly toasted. Serve garnished with lime and green onions.

larb-gai.title: Larb Gai (Spicy Thai Minced Chicken Salad)
steps: In a dry skillet on medium heat, toast 1 tbsp raw jasmine rice until deeply golden-brown and fragrant, then grind to a coarse powder (toasted rice powder/Khao Khua).
In a pan, add minced chicken and 2 tbsp water. Cook on medium heat, breaking up clumps, until chicken is fully cooked and dry.
Transfer cooked chicken to a mixing bowl. While warm, toss with fish sauce, lime juice, and chili flakes.
Add sliced shallots, mint leaves, and the toasted rice powder.
Toss everything together gently and serve warm alongside fresh cabbage leaves or sticky rice.

mushroom-risotto.title: Risotto ai Funghi (Creamy Mushroom Risotto)
steps: Warm 4 cups of vegetable stock in a separate saucepan and keep it simmering on low heat.
In a deep pan, heat olive oil and 1 tbsp butter. Sauté onions and mushrooms until lightly browned and soft.
Add rice directly to the pan. Toast and stir for 2 minutes until translucent at edges.
Pour in a ladle of hot stock. Stir constantly until the stock is fully absorbed by the rice.
Continue adding stock one ladle at a time, stirring continuously. Let the rice absorb the liquid before adding more. Repeat for 18-20 minutes until rice is tender but "al dente."
Turn off the heat. Stir in the remaining butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Let sit covered for 2 minutes to get rich and creamy.

beef-lasagna.title: Lasagna alla Bolognese (Italian Beef Lasagna)
steps: Sauté chopped onions and garlic. Add ground beef and brown for 5 minutes. Add tomato paste, tomato sauce, herbs, and simmer on low for 30 minutes to make the rich ragu.
Make Béchamel sauce: Melt butter, whisk in flour, and cook for 1 minute. Slowly pour in whole milk, whisking constantly, until a smooth, thick white sauce forms.
Boil lasagna pasta sheets until al dente, then drain.
In a large baking dish, spread a thin layer of meat ragu at the bottom. Lay pasta sheets, followed by a layer of ragu, Béchamel, and mozzarella cheese.
Repeat layering 3-4 times, finishing with a generous layer of Béchamel and mozzarella cheese on top.
Bake in preheated oven at 375°F (190°C) for 35-40 minutes until golden and bubbling on top. Let cool for 10 minutes before slicing.

tomato-bruschetta.title: Classic Tomato Bruschetta (Garlic Tomato Toast)
steps: Combine diced tomatoes, sweet basil, extra virgin olive oil, and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Let marinate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Grill or toast the bread slices on both sides until crispy and charred slightly.
Immediately rub the hot toasted bread surfaces with the cut side of a raw garlic clove (the bread acts as a grater, absorbing garlic flavor).
Spoon the marinated tomato basil mixture generously over the hot garlic-rubbed toast and serve warm.

pesto-pasta.title: Spaghetti al Pesto Genovese (Basil Pesto Pasta)
steps: Bring a pot of salted water to boil. Cook spaghetti until "al dente," reserving 1/2 cup pasta cooking water.
In a food processor, blend fresh sweet basil, garlic, toasted cashews, grated Parmesan, and a pinch of salt until coarsely chopped.
While blending on low speed, slowly drizzle in the extra virgin olive oil until a thick, bright green emulsion forms. Transfer to a bowl.
Drain pasta. Add spaghetti directly into the bowl with pesto (never cook pesto on heat, or it will turn black!).
Toss rapidly, adding 2-3 tbsp of hot pasta cooking water to create a creamy coating. Serve immediately.

osso-buco.title: Milanese Osso Buco (Braised Beef Shanks)
steps: Tie strings around shanks to keep shape. Dust shanks lightly with flour and sear in oil until deeply browned on both sides.
Remove shanks. In the same pan, sauté chopped onions, carrots, and garlic for 5 minutes.
Add tomato paste and 1 cup of dry white wine (or beef broth), scraping up browned bits.
Return shanks to the pot. Add beef broth to cover halfway. Cover tightly and simmer on low for 90 minutes until meat is falling off the bone.
Mix chopped parsley, lemon zest, and minced garlic together to create the fresh Gremolata topping.
Plate the shanks, ladle the rich cooking gravy on top, and scatter Gremolata over the beef. Serve warm.

caprese-salad.title: Insalata Caprese (Classic Italian Caprese Salad)
steps: Slice tomatoes and fresh mozzarella cheese into equal 1/3-inch thick rounds.
On a large flat plate, alternate overlapping slices of tomato and mozzarella cheese.
Tuck fresh sweet basil leaves between the cheese and tomato slices.
Drizzle extra virgin olive oil and a splash of balsamic vinegar (optional) in a spiral over the salad.
Sprinkle with flaky sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper right before serving.

minestrone-soup.title: Classic Italian Minestrone Soup
steps: Sauté chopped onions, garlic, and carrots in olive oil in a deep pot for 5 minutes.
Add potato cubes, zucchini, tomato paste, and 4 cups of vegetable stock. Bring to a boil.
Lower heat, cover, and simmer for 10 minutes until potatoes are partially cooked.
Add beans and the broken pasta pieces. Cook uncovered for 8-10 minutes until pasta is al dente.
Throw in the fresh chopped spinach. Simmer for 1 minute until wilted. Garnish with basil and serve.

chicken-enchiladas.title: Enchiladas Rojas (Mexican Red Chicken Enchiladas)
steps: Make the red sauce: Sauté minced garlic in a saucepan. Add tomato paste, chili powder, cumin powder, salt, and 1.5 cups of broth. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Mix the shredded chicken with 1/2 cup of red sauce and 1/2 cup of grated cheese.
Lightly fry each corn tortilla in a skillet with a splash of oil for 5 seconds on each side just to make them soft and pliable.
Dip a tortilla fully into the warm red sauce. Spoon chicken filling down the center, roll up tightly, and place seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the remaining red sauce generously over all rolled tortillas in the dish, and scatter cheese on top.
Bake in preheated oven at 375°F (190°C) for 15-20 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling.

pozole-rojo.title: Pozole Rojo (Mexican Hominy Soup)
steps: In a deep pot, boil chicken shanks in 6 cups of water with half an onion, garlic, and salt until tender. Shred chicken, discard bones, and keep broth.
Blend guajillo chili powder, 2 garlic cloves, chopped onions, oregano, and a cup of warm broth until a smooth red paste forms.
Pour the red chili paste back into the boiling chicken broth, passing through a strainer to discard pulp.
Add hominy corn (or rice substitute) and the shredded chicken into the red broth. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 20-30 minutes until hominy is tender and has absorbed the spices.
Serve hot, garnished with shredded cabbage, sliced radishes, dried oregano, and lime wedges.

chiles-rellenos.title: Chiles Rellenos (Mexican Cheese-Stuffed Peppers)
steps: Roast the green peppers directly over an open gas flame or under a broiler until the skin is entirely charred and black. Place in a bag to steam for 10 minutes.
Gently scrape off the charred skin. Cut a small slit in the side and carefully remove seeds. Stuff with mozzarella cheese sticks. Dust the outside with flour.
Beat egg whites with a hand mixer until stiff peaks form. Whisk in the egg yolks and a pinch of salt to create a fluffy batter.
Dip stuffed flour-dusted peppers fully into the fluffy egg batter.
Fry in 1 inch of hot oil for 2-3 minutes on each side until the batter is golden-brown and puffed. Drain on paper towels.
Make a light sauce by simmering tomato paste, minced garlic, and water for 5 minutes. Serve peppers hot on a bed of warm sauce.

beef-tamales.title: Beef Tamales (Mexican Steamed Masa Pastry)
steps: Soak corn husks in hot water for 30 minutes to make them soft and pliable.
Make Masa dough: Beat lard/ghee with a mixer until fluffy. Gradually add corn flour (Masa Harina), salt, and warm beef broth until a smooth spreadable paste forms.
Cook shredded beef with minced garlic and red chili paste for 5 minutes to create the filling.
Pat a corn husk dry. Spread 2 tbsp of Masa dough in a thin square on the wide end of the husk. Spoon 1 tbsp filling down the center.
Fold the sides of the husk together so the Masa closes over the filling. Fold the narrow tail up. Secure tightly.
Stand tamales upright in a steamer basket. Cover and steam for 50 minutes until the Masa pulls away clean from the husk. Let rest for 10 minutes and serve.

chicken-mole.title: Mole Poblano (Chicken in Savory Chili Chocolate Sauce)
steps: Toast peanuts, sesame seeds, cinnamon, and cloves in a dry skillet until fragrant.
Sauté chopped onions and garlic. Blend with toasted seeds, chili powder, spices, and warm broth into a thick, completely smooth paste.
Fry the thick Mole paste in a tablespoon of oil on low heat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in the Mexican chocolate substitute (sugar-palm) and a splash of broth. Simmer on low until chocolate melts and integrates.
Add the cooked chicken pieces into the dark Mole sauce. Simmer gently on low for 15-20 minutes until chicken is deeply infused.
Serve warm, garnished with toasted sesame seeds, alongside warm tortillas.

shrimp-ceviche.title: Mexican Shrimp Ceviche
steps: Place raw shrimp pieces in a non-reactive glass bowl. Pour fresh lime juice over them until completely submerged.
Cover and place in the fridge for 20-30 minutes. The shrimp will absorb the acid, turning opaque and pink.
Drain half the excess lime juice. Add diced tomatoes, red onions, minced jalapeño, and salt.
Gently fold in chopped fresh cilantro and a drizzle of olive oil.
Serve cold with crispy corn tostadas or tortilla chips.

elote.title: Elote (Mexican Street Corn)
steps: Preheat a grill or heavy iron skillet to medium-high heat.
Grill the corn cobs, turning occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until lightly charred on all sides.
Brush each hot grilled corn cob immediately with a generous layer of mayonnaise.
Roll the coated corn cobs in the grated cheese until heavily covered.
Dust heavily with chili powder, sprinkle chopped cilantro on top, squeeze fresh lime, and enjoy warm.

churros.title: Mexican Churros with Chocolate Dip
steps: In a pot, combine 1 cup water, butter, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Pour in flour all at once and stir vigorously until a thick dough ball forms. Remove from heat.
Let the dough cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the egg until completely smooth and glossy.
Transfer dough to a piping bag fitted with a closed star nozzle.
Pipe 6-inch strips of dough directly into hot frying oil, cutting the end with scissors.
Fry for 3-4 minutes on each side until deeply golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Roll the hot fried churros immediately in cinnamon sugar and serve warm with chocolate dip.

hong-shao-rou.title: Hong Shao Rou (Red Braised Pork Belly)
steps: Place pork belly cubes in cold water, bring to a boil, and blanch for 3 minutes to remove impurities. Drain and pat dry.
Add 1 tbsp oil and 2 tbsp sugar to a cold wok. Heat on low, stirring constantly, until sugar melts and turns into a light brown caramel syrup.
Carefully add the blanched pork belly cubes. Stir-fry quickly on medium heat for 2 minutes to coat each piece in the caramel glaze.
Pour in Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and enough warm water to fully cover the pork. Add ginger slices, scallions, cinnamon, and 1 star anise.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 50-60 minutes until pork is fork-tender and melting.
Remove the lid, discard aromatics, and turn the heat to high. Sauté, stirring constantly, for 5 minutes until the sauce reduces into a thick, sticky glaze that clings to the pork.

yangzhou-fried-rice.title: Yangzhou Fried Rice
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok. Sauté the diced pork and shrimp for 2 minutes until cooked. Set aside.
Pour egg into the hot wok. Sauté for 10 seconds, immediately adding the cold jasmine rice before the egg fully cooks.
Stir-fry vigorously, breaking up clumps of rice with the spatula, ensuring the egg wraps the grains.
Add light soy sauce, salt, sweet corn, and green peas. Sauté on medium-high heat for 2 minutes.
Return the cooked pork and shrimp to the wok, tossing to combine thoroughly.
Toss in the chopped green onions, stir-fry on high heat for 1 minute until fragrant and completely dry, and serve.

tomato-scrambled-eggs.title: Tomato Scrambled Eggs (Fan Qie Chao Dan)
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok on high heat. Pour in beaten eggs and stir-fry for just 30-40 seconds until soft curds form. Remove immediately while still slightly wet.
Add 1 tsp oil to the same wok. Sauté sliced garlic and white scallion parts for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add tomato wedges. Cook on medium heat for 3 minutes, pressing them gently with a spatula to release their sweet juice and form a light sauce.
Stir in sugar, salt, and 2 tbsp of water. Simmer for 1 minute.
Return the scrambled eggs to the wok. Swirl to combine and coat them in the sweet tomato sauce without breaking the egg curds.
Turn off heat. Scatter the green scallion parts and serve hot with plain steamed rice.

dan-dan-noodles.title: Sichuan Dan Dan Noodles
steps: Topping: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok. Fry ground meat until dry and crispy.
Add pickled mustard greens (Ya Cai) and 1 tsp soy sauce to the meat. Stir-fry for 2 minutes and set aside.
Sauce: In a large bowl, whisk together Chinese sesame paste (or peanut butter), sesame oil, soy sauce, minced garlic, sugar, and chili oil to create a thick paste.
Boil wheat noodles according to package instructions. Drain, keeping 1/2 cup of hot noodle cooking water.
Whisk the hot noodle cooking water into the sesame-peanut sauce bowl to dilute it into a creamy, pourable sauce.
Assemble: Divide the sauce among serving bowls, place hot boiled noodles on top, scatter the crispy pork topping, and garnish with crushed peanuts.

di-san-xian.title: Di San Xian (Three Earthly Treasures)
steps: Toss eggplant chunks with 1 tsp salt and let them sit for 15 minutes to squeeze out excess moisture. Pat dry.
Sauce: Mix 2 tbsp soy sauce, sugar, salt, and 1 tsp cornstarch with 4 tbsp water in a bowl.
Heat 4 tbsp oil in a wok. Fry potato wedges on medium heat for 6-8 minutes until golden-brown and crispy-edged. Remove and set aside.
In the same wok, shallow fry the eggplant chunks for 4 minutes until soft. Add green bell pepper chunks for the final 1 minute. Remove all and drain.
Discard excess oil, leaving 1 tsp. Sauté minced garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return potatoes, eggplant, and peppers to the wok. Stir in the glaze sauce. Sauté on high heat for 1-2 minutes until the sauce bubbles, thickens, and glazes the vegetables.

beef-broccoli.title: Classic Chinese Beef with Broccoli
steps: Marinate sliced beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, and 1 tsp cornstarch for 15 minutes to tenderize (velveting).
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling water for exactly 1 minute, then plunge them into ice water to keep crisp-tender. Drain.
In a bowl, mix oyster sauce, remaining soy sauce, 1 tsp cornstarch, and 4 tbsp water to make the stir-fry glaze.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a smoking-hot wok. Sear beef slices in a single layer for 1 minute without moving, then toss for another 30 seconds until just browned. Set aside.
Add 1 tsp oil. Sauté garlic and ginger for 30 seconds. Return beef and blanched broccoli to the wok.
Pour in the glaze sauce. Toss on high heat for 1 minute until the sauce bubbles and coats the beef and broccoli. Serve hot.

wonton-soup.title: Clear Wonton Soup
steps: Combine ground meat, minced shrimp, ginger, chopped scallion, soy sauce, sesame oil, and salt in a bowl. Mix vigorously in one direction until cohesive.
Place 1 teaspoon of filling in the center of a wonton wrapper. Fold into a triangle, dampening the edges, and squeeze the two corners together to seal (noodle fold). Repeat.
Bring 4 cups of chicken broth to a gentle boil with a slice of ginger and a dash of soy sauce.
In a separate pot of boiling water, boil wontons for 3-4 minutes. They will float to the surface when cooked.
Drain wontons and transfer them directly into serving bowls.
Ladle the seasoned hot chicken broth over the wontons, drizzle sesame oil, and scatter fresh green onions.

char-siu.title: Char Siu (Chinese BBQ Pork)
steps: Prick pork shoulder strips with a fork. Marinate with hoisin sauce, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, five-spice, and garlic for at least 4 hours (or overnight).
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C). Place a wire rack over a foil-lined baking sheet and lay the pork strips on the rack.
Roast for 20 minutes. Keep the remaining marinade in a small bowl.
Mix the honey with 2 tbsp of the remaining marinade to create a sticky glaze.
Flip the pork strips, brush heavily with the honey glaze, and roast for another 15 minutes until charred and caramelized at the edges.
Let the meat rest for 10 minutes before slicing thinly. Serve with steamed jasmine rice.

mutton-biryani-sindhi.title: Sindhi Mutton Biryani
steps: Marinate mutton in yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani spices, and salt for 1-2 hours.
Heat oil in a pot. Fry sliced onions until deeply golden. Sauté marinated mutton and potato halves for 10 minutes.
Add 2 cups of water, cover, and simmer on medium heat for 30 minutes until mutton is tender.
Boil basmati rice with whole spices (bay leaf, cloves) until 70% cooked (still has a hard core). Drain.
Dum Layering: In a deep pot, layer the mutton and potato curry at the bottom. Cover with parboiled rice. Scatter fresh mint, coriander leaves, lemon slices, and saffron milk.
Seal the lid tightly with foil and cook on low heat on a skillet (tawa) for 20 minutes (Dum). Fluff and serve.

dal-chawal.title: Pakistani Dal Chawal
steps: In a pot, combine red and yellow lentils, 4 cups of water, garlic paste, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Bring to a boil.
Lower heat, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the lentils are completely soft and mushy.
Whisk the dal with a hand blender or wooden spoon to create a smooth, creamy texture.
Tadka: Heat ghee in a small pan. Fry sliced garlic, cumin seeds, and green chili until garlic turns golden-brown and seeds crackle.
Pour the sizzling tadka directly into the boiling dal pot (be careful of splashes) and cover immediately to lock in the aroma.
Serve piping hot over a bed of steamed basmati rice with pickle.

chapli-kabab.title: Peshawari Chapli Kabab
steps: Mix ground beef with minced onion, tomato, ginger-garlic paste, chopped green chili, crushed pomegranate seeds, salt, and crushed coriander seeds.
Add a beaten egg and 2 tbsp cornmeal/flour to bind the meat mixture. Knead vigorously like bread dough for 5 minutes until sticky.
Divide meat into large balls. Flatten them between damp palms into thin, large discs (approx. 6 inches). Press a round slice of tomato firmly into the center of each kabab.
Heat animal fat or ghee in a shallow frying pan until very hot.
Gently slide in the kababs. Shallow fry on medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes on each side until dark brown and crispy on the edges.
Drain excess oil and serve hot with naan and mint raita.

aloo-keema.title: Aloo Keema (Minced Beef & Potatoes)
steps: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a pot. Sauté chopped onions until golden-brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and ground beef. Sauté on high heat for 5 minutes, breaking the meat clumps until it changes color.
Stir in tomato paste, chili powder, turmeric, cumin, and salt. Cook for 3 minutes until oil separates from the masala.
Add cubed potatoes and 1 cup of water. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 12-15 minutes until potatoes are fork-tender.
Stir in garam masala and freshly ground black pepper. Sauté uncovered for 2 minutes to dry any excess moisture.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and chopped green chilies, and serve with flatbread.

siri-paye.title: Pakistani Siri Paye (Slow-Cooked Trotters Stew)
steps: Trotters Prep: Sauté cleaned trotters in 1 tbsp ghee with a pinch of turmeric for 5 minutes, then drain to remove strong odors.
Heat remaining ghee in a large pot. Sauté onion puree and ginger-garlic paste until moisture evaporates.
Add cardamom, cinnamon, chili powder, and fennel powder. Cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in yogurt and the trotters. Sear on medium-high heat for 5 minutes.
Pour in 8 cups of water. Bring to a boil, cover tightly, and cook on extremely low heat for 6-8 hours (or pressure cook for 60 minutes) until trotters are tender and gravy is gelatinous.
Serve warm, topped with fresh coriander and lemon halves.

sheer-khurma.title: Festive Sheer Khurma
steps: Heat ghee in a pan. Toast slivered almonds, cashews, pistachios, and dried dates for 2 minutes until lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same ghee, add the crushed vermicelli. Toast on low heat for 3-4 minutes until it turns a beautiful golden-brown.
Boil whole milk in a large pot. Simmer on medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for 15 minutes to reduce slightly.
Add the toasted vermicelli and sugar to the boiling milk. Cook on medium-low heat for 10 minutes until vermicelli is soft.
Stir in the toasted nuts, dates, and crushed cardamom. Simmer for another 5 minutes until the pudding thickens.
Serve warm or chill in the refrigerator before serving. Garnish with remaining toasted nuts.

chicken-tikka-pakistani.title: Charcoal Chicken Tikka (Pakistani Style)
steps: Rub chicken quarters with lemon juice, salt, and 1 tsp chili powder. Let sit for 10 minutes.
Whisk yogurt with garlic-ginger paste, garam masala, remaining chili powder, and a drop of orange food color (optional). Coat chicken quarters and marinate for 2 hours.
Place quarters on skewers. Grill over hot charcoal or bake in a 425°F (220°C) oven for 20 minutes, flipping once.
Brush heavily with melted ghee or butter during the final 5 minutes of grilling to keep it juicy.
Smoke: Place a small metal bowl inside the chicken pot, put a burning red-hot charcoal piece in it, pour 1 tsp oil over the coal, and cover tightly for 3 minutes.
Serve piping hot with onions, mint chutney, and fresh limes.

halwa-puri-cholay.title: Sunday Halwa Puri & Cholay Breakfast
steps: Puri Dough: Knead flour with 1 tbsp oil, salt, and water into a smooth, firm dough. Rest covered for 20 minutes.
Cholay Curry: Sauté chopped onions and ginger-garlic paste. Add boiled chickpeas, tomato paste, turmeric, chili powder, and cumin. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Halwa Syrup: Boil 1 cup sugar in 3 cups of water with crushed cardamom seeds for 5 minutes until fully dissolved.
Halwa: Melt ghee. Toast semolina on low heat for 5-6 minutes until fragrant and golden-sandy. Carefully pour in hot sugar syrup. Whisk on low heat until thick and creamy.
Puri: Roll dough into thin, small circles. Deep fry in extremely hot oil, pressing down gently until they instantly puff up. Flip and drain.
Serve puffed hot puris with warm chickpea curry and sweet halwa.
